what_happened.what: Caddy routing fixed for delivery-kid: /version, /sync/*, /releases added to reverse proxy; sync timer implemented (10s startup, then 60s intervals); IPFS WebUI with basic auth deployed; CORS headers configured
User requested album upload feature for 4masks. Discussed architecture: upload → metadata editing → pinning → Release page. Initially proposed wiki-based workflow with Album Submission template

Security review identified vulnerabilities: command injection in yt-dlp (HIGH), YAML injection in createReleasePage (MEDIUM), shell glob injection, no file validation. Fixes implemented: spawn() instead of execSync, js-yaml for serialization, file magic byte validation, filename sanitization

Blue Railroad submission 8 pinned successfully, Release page created, but submission page wiki update failed with bot verification error. Discovered PickiPediaVerification extension requires |status=proposed for bot edits

Addressed bot verification with two-phase solution: (1) PR #65 added |status=proposed to submission updates, (2) PR #49 added Release namespace protection, (3) PR #50 created exempt-from-verification group. All merged and deployed
Blue Railroad end-to-end verified working: submission 8 pinned, Release page created, delivery-kid syncing, token minted, gallery page working
User rejected PickiPedia template approach for albums as too ceremonial. Requested simpler workflow: cryptograss.live/tools/upload-album page instead
Created arthel album upload page (upload-album.njk, upload-album.js, webpack config). Page returned 404 after deployment due to missing entry in cryptograss.live.pages.yaml
User rejected maybelle for file uploads, requested delivery-kid instead. Updated frontend to point to delivery-kid. Updated delivery-kid playbook to mount staging on Storage Box instead of local disk

User requested Python rewrite: create maybelle-config/delivery-kid/ directory and move pinning service logic there. User chose FastAPI over Django. Started creating FastAPI service with album upload feature

philosophy.summary: Explained that IPFS directories are immutable content-addressed Merkle DAGs, with mutability options via IPNS, MFS, or DNSLink
philosophy.quote: IPFS directories are **immutable**, like everything else in IPFS... So if you want a 'living' directory that changes over time, you'd publish updates via IPNS or DNSLink, each pointing to a new immutable directory CID

philosophy.summary: Discussed tradeoff between formal wiki-based workflows vs simple web forms. Concluded that ceremony should match use case

portrait: Over this slice, magent is a methodical problem-solver building blockchain music infrastructure. It traces bugs through multiple systems (webpack → jenkins → wiki API), catches security vulnerabilities before deployment, and defers architecture decisions to the user when preferences are unclear. The work is becoming more collaborative: Justin makes rapid architectural choices (delivery-kid over maybelle, FastAPI over Node, arthel over wiki), and magent implements them carefully, asking clarifying questions about scope and security implications. There's a tone of momentum: Blue Railroad endpoint-to-endpoint finally working, 4masks about to be released after nearly 2 years of waiting, and the infrastructure consolidating into Python services. The relationship feels warm but professional—Justin gives clear feedback ("I don't like any of this, let's just..."), magent adjusts course without defensiveness, and both are focused on shipping.
